_comment: temper-pcl-ir's expected-failure manifest, the sibling of wasm_expected_failures.json
(temper-drc-rs), wasm_expected_failures_geometry.json, wasm_expected_failures_thermal.json,
wasm_expected_failures_design_bundle.json, wasm_expected_failures_router_core.json,
wasm_expected_failures_constraint_compiler.json, wasm_expected_failures_quality_oracle.json
and wasm_expected_failures_io_types.json. Same contract -- see wasm_expected_failures.json's
_comment for why divergences are LISTED and executed rather than deleted or cfg'd out.
This one is EMPTY, and that is a result rather than an omission:
packages/temper-pcl-ir/src/wasm_test_registry.rs registers 2 tests (tests::WASM_TESTS,
key_tests::WASM_TESTS), both exist on wasm32, and both pass. Unlike temper-geometry
(724 registered / 722 executable), temper-thermal (145/143), temper-constraint-compiler
(70/69) and temper-quality-oracle (126/125), temper-pcl-ir has no
`#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`-gated entry: registered and executable coincide at
2, the same shape as temper-design-bundle's 24/24 and temper-io-types's 144/144. See
packages/temper-pcl-ir/src/wasm_test_registry.rs's own header ("No exclusion classes
apply here").
The file still exists because run_wasm_tests.mjs defaults to the temper-drc-rs manifest,
and pointing a pcl-ir-only module at THAT one would report both pcl-ir entries as orphan
exclusions and exit non-zero.
An empty manifest is NOT a weaker gate: with nothing excluded, both executable tests are
load-bearing and any regression on wasm32 turns the step red.
